name: performance

findings.message: Every cycle iteration now performs two `locked_state_update` calls — the new `_cycle_state_write_iter_start` at the top of each iteration plus the pre-existing `_cycle_state_write_iter_atomic` at the end — each acquiring flock, spawning jq for JSON validation, spawning jq for the transform, and doing an atomic rename, doubling per-iteration blocking state I/O on the cycle hot path.
findings.quote:
_cycle_state_write_iter_start "$state_file" "$cycle_id" "$iter" \
            || warn "cycle-orchestrator: failed to write iter-start state for cycle=$cycle_id iter=$iter (a resume may start at the wrong iteration)"

findings.message: `_artifact_persist_put_back` spawns a subshell and an external `dirname` process for every artifact file copied during resume rehydration; replacing `$(dirname "$to/$rel")` with the pure-bash parameter expansion `"${to}/${rel%/*}"` eliminates O(files) subprocess pairs.

In the DSCMBR-1 block of `_cycle_iter_dispatch`, each already-complete cycle member triggers five separate jq subprocess spawns (two reads from the state file, one `jq -cn` to build the entry, one `jq -c` to merge it into the blob, and one re-read for the verdict); a single jq invocation could extract both `stage_statuses[$s]` and `stage_verdicts[$s]` simultaneously, reducing the total to one per skipped member.
